001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007import java.util.Arrays;
008
009/**
010 * The response the pump sent to a signed CONTROL request, written immediately after the
011 * {@link ControlRequestHistoryLog} for that request (its {@code requestOpCode} is this record's
012 * {@code responseOpCode} minus one in 3692/3692 records across both capture sets).
013 *
014 * <p>The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum
015 * do not name this opcode.
016 *
017 * <p>Only some commands are answered with this record. Observed response opcodes: 133
018 * UserInteraction, 135 SetMaxBolusLimit, 137 SetMaxBasalLimit, 155 ResumePumping, 157
019 * SuspendPumping, 167 StopTempRate, 195 CgmHighLowAlert, 197 CgmRiseFallAlert, 199
020 * CgmOutOfRangeAlert, 211 SetQuickBolusSettings, 213 SetPumpAlertSnooze, 215 ChangeTimeDate, 217
021 * SetBgReminder, 221 SetSiteChangeReminder, 223 SetLowInsulinAlert, 225 SetAutoOffAlert, 229
022 * SetPumpSounds, 237 SetActiveIDP and 245 PlaySound. SetTempRate is answered with
023 * {@link SetTempRateResponseHistoryLog} instead; the cartridge/fill commands and
024 * DismissNotification use other opcodes as well.
025 *
026 * <p>Byte 11 and bytes 13-25 are zero in every Mobi record examined; they are kept as raw
027 * accessors. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/145.
028 */
029@HistoryLogProps(
030    opCode = 300,
031    displayName = "Control Response",
032    internalName = ""
033)
034public class ControlResponseHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
035
036    private int responseOpCode;
037    private int unknown11;
038    private int status;
039    private byte[] unknownTail;
040
041    public ControlResponseHistoryLog() {}
042    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int unknown11, int status, byte[] unknownTail) {
043        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
044        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, responseOpCode, unknown11, status, unknownTail);
045        this.responseOpCode = responseOpCode;
046        this.unknown11 = unknown11;
047        this.status = status;
048        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(this.cargo, 13, 26);
049    }
050
051    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int status) {
052        this(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, responseOpCode, 0, status, new byte[13]);
053    }
054
055    public ControlResponseHistoryLog(int responseOpCode, int status) {
056        this(0, 0, responseOpCode, status);
057    }
058
059    public int typeId() {
060        return 300;
061    }
062
063    /**
064     * <table border="1">
065     * <caption>Parsed fields for ControlResponseHistoryLog:</caption>
066     * <tr><td><code>responseOpCode</code></td><td><code>raw[10] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
067     * <tr><td><code>unknown11</code></td><td><code>raw[11] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
068     * <tr><td><code>status</code></td><td><code>raw[12] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
069     * <tr><td><code>unknownTail</code></td><td><code>Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 13, 26)</code></td></tr>
070     * </table>
071     */
072    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
073        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
074        this.cargo = raw;
075        parseBase(raw);
076        this.responseOpCode = raw[10] & 0xFF;
077        this.unknown11 = raw[11] & 0xFF;
078        this.status = raw[12] & 0xFF;
079        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 13, 26);
080    }
081
082    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int responseOpCode, int unknown11, int status, byte[] unknownTail) {
083        Validate.isTrue(unknownTail.length == 13, "unknownTail must be 13 bytes");
084        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
085            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(300, 0),
086            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
087            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
088            new byte[]{ (byte) responseOpCode, (byte) unknown11, (byte) status },
089            unknownTail));
090    }
091
092    /**
093     * The opcode of the response the pump sent, as an unsigned byte (the pumpX2 response
094     * {@code opCode} ANDed with 0xFF), which is the request's opcode plus one: for example 167
095     * is StopTempRateResponse and 155 is ResumePumpingResponse.
096     *
097     * @return the unsigned opcode of the response
098     */
099    public int getResponseOpCode() {
100        return responseOpCode;
101    }
102
103    /**
104     * The status byte of that response: 0 on success. Every nonzero value checked against the
105     * app log matched a response that reported a failure (for example a ResumePumping request
106     * rejected with status 1 and retried successfully a second later); StopTempRate responses
107     * logged as successful all read 0 here (1734/1734).
108     *
109     * @return the response status, 0 for success
110     */
111    public int getStatus() {
112        return status;
113    }
114
115    /**
116     * @return byte 11, which was 0 in every record examined
117     */
118    public int getUnknown11() {
119        return unknown11;
120    }
121
122    /**
123     * Bytes 13-25. They are zero on the Mobi. In 17 t:slim X2 records answering
124     * UserInteraction (response opcode 133), bytes 15-17 of the record (index 2-4 here) held the
125     * low 24 bits of the record's own pumpTimeSec; their purpose is unknown.
126     *
127     * @return a copy of bytes 13-25
128     */
129    public byte[] getUnknownTail() {
130        return Arrays.copyOf(unknownTail, unknownTail.length);
131    }
132}
